name: China

facts.religion: Mostly non-religious, with Buddhist, folk, Christian and Muslim minorities

snapshot: Xi Jinping's purge reached the top of the army in 2026, when China's senior general was put under investigation, as Beijing bet its new five-year plan on chips and AI.
culture: China's civilisation stretches back more than three millennia, and Confucian values of family, education and hierarchy still shape daily life. The Spring Festival triggers the world's largest annual migration. Mandarin is promoted nationwide, while Cantonese, Shanghainese and minority languages persist. Social media platforms like WeChat and Douyin are woven into everything from payment to dating.
society: China lifted hundreds of millions out of poverty and became the world's manufacturing centre and leader in electric vehicles, solar panels and batteries. Its population is shrinking and ageing, youth unemployment is high, and a property crash has hit household wealth. Xinjiang's Uyghurs and Tibetans face mass surveillance and repression.

story: Xi Jinping has spent 14 years making himself the most powerful Chinese leader since Mao, purging more than 200,000 officials in an anti-corruption drive that critics say doubles as a loyalty test. In 2026 the purge reached the very top of the military he commands.

On 24 January, the Defence Ministry announced that Zhang Youxia, 75, the senior vice chairman of the Central Military Commission, China's top general and a princeling whose father fought alongside Xi's, was under investigation for "serious violations of discipline and law" (NPR via WJCT). The other vice chairman, He Weidong, had already been expelled in October 2025. That means both of Xi's top uniformed deputies have now fallen, along with dozens of generals, including those running the nuclear rocket force. Analysts disagree on whether this reflects real corruption, disloyalty or Xi's worry about the army's readiness for a possible Taiwan conflict, but it has left the People's Liberation Army's command in turmoil just as Xi wants it ready. In March the National People's Congress approved the 15th Five-Year Plan for 2026-30, focused on self-reliance in chips and technology and on AI as an engine of growth, to shield China from US tariffs and export controls (TaiwanPlus). Trump visited Beijing in May, and Xi is expected in Washington this autumn. Beijing has also kept up pressure on Japan over Prime Minister Takaichi's Taiwan remarks.
briefing.power: A one-party state. The Communist Party controls the government, army, courts and media. Xi is party general secretary, state president and chairman of the Central Military Commission; the seven-member Politburo Standing Committee is the top decision body. The National People's Congress is a rubber-stamp legislature.
briefing.holders: Xi Jinping, in power since 2012; Premier Li Qiang.
